label: Control and governance frameworks
summary: Voluntary or contract-driven control sets (NIST CSF, 800-53, 800-171, AI RMF, CIS Controls, COBIT). None gives a certificate by itself, so the onboarding fixes what the framework is applied to and how it is tailored: a profile scope, a system boundary and categorization, a CUI scope, an AI inventory, an implementation group or the COBIT design factors.

requires_org.reason: The scope is drawn around systems.
CIS, CMMC and NIST scoping start from an inventory.
Priorities and targets follow the board's risk tolerance.

source.ref: NIST CSF 2.0 Organizational Profiles (SP 1301 step 1: scope), SP 800-37 Prepare tasks, CIS Controls Implementation Groups, COBIT 2019 implementation phase 1 (drivers)

fields.label: Purpose
fields.note: Why the framework is being used. It decides how formal the evidence has to be and who reviews the result.

fields.label: Scope statement
fields.note: What the framework is applied to: units, data, technology, products or suppliers, and what is left out. SP 1301 asks for this first, and a profile that is too coarse to act on is the usual mistake.

fields.label: Units
fields.note: Departments inside the scope.

fields.label: Sites
fields.note: Sites inside the scope.

fields.label: Systems
fields.note: Systems inside the scope, picked from the organisation profile.

fields.label: Scope owner
fields.note: Who owns the scope and answers questions about it.

fields.label: Approver
fields.note: Who approves the scope and the target. The framework names no sign-off role, but an executive approval is good practice.

source.ref: NIST CSF 2.0 (CSWP 29) and SP 1301: current and target profiles, tiers, community profiles, GOVERN context GV.OC

fields.label: Governance tier
fields.note: Target tier for risk governance. Tiers are optional and are not a maturity score; set governance and management tiers separately.

fields.label: Management tier
fields.note: Target tier for risk management.

fields.label: Community profile
fields.note: A sector or use-case baseline to start from, or write 'none'.

fields.label: Rating scale
fields.note: Scale for current and target ratings and for priority. Fix it before rating.

fields.label: Requirements listed
fields.note: Legal, regulatory and contractual requirements were reviewed in the organisation profile (GV.OC-03).

fields.label: System name

source.ref: NIST RMF (SP 800-37 Rev 2): prepare, categorize, select; FIPS 199; SP 800-53B baselines; roles crosswalk

fields.note: The system the authorization is for. The boundary is drawn per system.

fields.label: Authorization boundary
fields.note: What is inside the boundary, with its connections and support systems. A boundary drawn around the product but not its supporting systems is the usual mistake.

fields.label: Information types
fields.note: Information types processed, each with an impact level for confidentiality, integrity and availability (FIPS 199). The system level is the highest of them.

fields.label: Baseline
fields.note: Chosen from the highest impact value (SP 800-53B). Categorize first, then select.

fields.label: Privacy baseline
fields.note: Add the privacy baseline when the system processes personal information, whatever the security level.

fields.label: Parameter values
fields.note: Organisation-defined parameters in Rev 5 become part of the control and are assessed; set them before assessment.

fields.label: Authorizing official
fields.note: Accepts the risk and approves the boundary. Cannot be delegated and cannot also be the system owner.

fields.label: System owner
fields.note: Leads categorization and answers for the system.

fields.label: Control assessor
fields.note: The authorizing official decides how independent the assessor must be.

fields.label: CUI categories

source.ref: NIST SP 800-171 and 32 CFR part 170 (CMMC): CUI scoping, asset categories, SSP, POA&M, SPRS

fields.note: The CUI categories handled and the contract clause or marking that proves it. Map where CUI is created, stored, processed and sent.

fields.label: CMMC level
fields.note: From the contract. The status can be Conditional or Final; a Level 2 pass also covers Level 1 for the same scope.

fields.label: CAGE codes
fields.note: All CAGE codes the scope covers. The SPRS entry lists them.

fields.label: Assets categorised
fields.note: The inventory is split into CUI assets, security protection assets, contractor risk managed assets, specialized assets and out-of-scope assets. Security tools that never touch CUI are still in scope.

fields.label: Service providers
fields.note: External service providers and cloud providers. A provider that handles CUI must meet FedRAMP requirements; record a customer responsibility matrix.

fields.label: SSP status
fields.note: The system security plan is the reference for the whole scope; a self-score without one is not accepted.

fields.label: C3PAO
fields.note: The accredited third-party assessment organisation.

fields.label: Affirming official
fields.note: The senior official who makes the annual affirmation.

fields.label: AI systems

source.ref: NIST AI RMF 1.0: GOVERN 1.6 inventory, MAP 1 and 2 context and categorization, MAP 4 third-party components

fields.note: Every AI system in or out of scope, including bought and embedded AI. Starting without Map context is the usual mistake.

fields.label: AI risk tolerance
fields.note: The stated tolerance that sets how deep risk management goes (MAP 1.5, GOVERN 1.3).

fields.label: Accountable executive
fields.note: Executive leadership takes responsibility for decisions about AI risk (GOVERN 2.3).

fields.label: AI actors
fields.note: People or teams per lifecycle stage: design, development, deployment, operation, test and evaluation, impact assessment.

fields.label: Implementation group
fields.note: Each group includes the one before. Everyone starts with IG1; IG2 suits dedicated IT staff and sensitive client data; IG3 suits specialists, regulated or targeted organisations.

fields.label: Why this group
fields.note: Link the choice to data sensitivity, staff, regulation and threats. Choosing IG3 for prestige or IG1 to avoid work is the usual mistake.

fields.label: Assessment tool
fields.note: How safeguards will be rated.

fields.label: Strategy

source.ref: COBIT 2019 design guide: the eleven design factors and the implementation roadmap

fields.note: Design factor 1, enterprise strategy archetype.

fields.label: Enterprise goals
fields.note: Design factor 2: the top enterprise goals, by scorecard dimension.

fields.label: Risk profile
fields.note: Design factors 3 and 4: the risk profile and I&T-related issues.

fields.label: Threat landscape
fields.note: Design factor 5.

fields.label: Compliance needs
fields.note: Design factor 6.

fields.label: Role of IT
fields.note: Design factor 7.

fields.label: Sourcing model
fields.note: Design factor 8.

fields.label: IT methods
fields.note: Design factor 9.

fields.label: Technology adoption
fields.note: Design factor 10.

fields.label: Enterprise size
fields.note: Design factor 11.

fields.label: Drivers
fields.note: Why governance is being improved and what triggered it (implementation phase 1). Skipping the drivers and the sponsor is the usual mistake.

source.ref: SP 1301 steps 3 to 5 (create, analyse gaps, implement); CIS CSAT; COBIT phases 2 to 7

fields.label: Assessment method
fields.note: Who rates the controls. Ratings need an evidence trail whichever is chosen.

fields.label: First assessment
fields.note: Target date for the first complete assessment.

fields.label: Review cycle
fields.note: How often the assessment is repeated. The frameworks fix no cycle; regulators and customers often do.

gate.label: Authorizing official and system owner are different people
gate.hint: The authorizing official cannot also own the system.

gate.label: A baseline is chosen after categorization
gate.hint: Categorize the information types first, then choose Low, Moderate or High.

gate.label: A system security plan exists
gate.hint: Start the plan before any self-score.

gate.label: Assets are split into the five categories
At least one AI system is listed
gate.hint: List AI systems before mapping them.

gate.label: Requirements were reviewed
gate.hint: Review obligations in the organisation profile first.

gate.label: Scope owner and approver are different people
gate.hint: Someone other than the owner approves the scope.
